summary: Makes onSave async so that it writes the whole note store to data/notes.json after each save.

findings.title: Async onSave breaks the synchronous dispatch caller
findings.problem: onSave now returns a Promise, and dispatch in src/router.js:7 passes it on without awaiting it. The request handler in src/main.js:9 then passes that Promise to res.end, which accepts only a string or a Buffer.
findings.consequence: Each POST /save request makes res.end throw a TypeError inside the request listener, and the Node process crashes. Nobody handles the writeFile Promise either, so a failed write also becomes an unhandled rejection.
findings.fix: Make dispatch async and have the request handler await it with a catch that sends an error response. Another option is to keep onSave synchronous and handle the snapshot write separately.

findings.title: Snapshot write has no covering test
findings.problem: onSave now writes the store to data/notes.json and returns a Promise. No test in the repository exercises onSave or that write.
findings.consequence: A test that calls save through dispatch would have caught the broken response path. Without tests, regressions in onSave reach users unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a test that calls dispatch with save and checks both the response text and the written snapshot.
